question: What's the PSI in Tampines right now?
name: Claude
answer:
I couldn't get a live reading, but the latest figure I found for Tampines is **173 (24-hour PSI), which is in the "unhealthy" range.** That's from 2pm on 17 Oct. Tampines is in Singapore's East region, so I'm using the East reading.

**Readings at 2pm on 17 Oct:**
- The 24-hour PSI was "unhealthy" in every region: central 184, north 135, south 154, east 173 and west 185.
- The 1-hour PM2.5 reading was 159 in the east. That's in the "high" band. PM2.5 shows conditions over the last hour better than the 24-hour PSI does.

**Recent trend:**
- The day before, on 16 Oct, Singapore's 24-hour PSI was in the "very unhealthy" range, and the East hit 205.
- The National Environment Agency (NEA) said the PSI on 17 Oct could range from 150 to 230, which spans "unhealthy" to "very unhealthy."
- This is Singapore's 12th straight day of unhealthy air, the longest run since the 2015 haze crisis.

For the current reading, check NEA's haze website (haze.gov.sg) or the myENV app, since both update every hour. While the PSI is this high, cut down on time outdoors, especially for children, older people and anyone with heart or lung problems. Wear an N95 mask if you have to go out.

SINGAPORE; Hazy conditions persisted into the afternoon of Oct 17, even as the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) in central Singapore dipped back into the “unhealthy” band after remaining in the “very unhealthy” range the previous day.

At 2pm, the 24-hour PSI was in the “unhealthy” range in all regions: central (184), north (135), south (154), east (173) and west (185).

Meanwhile, hourly PM2.5 readings entered the “high” range in the west at 158 at 11am, followed by the central and southern regions at noon and the east at 2pm.

At 2pm, hourly PM2.5 readings stood at 243 in the west, 179 in the central region, 162 in the south and 159 in the east. The figure remained in the “elevated” range in the north at 91.

The central region was worst hit on Oct 16, when the 24-hour PSI remained in the “very unhealthy” range throughout the day, peaking at a seasonal high of 229 between 3pm and 4pm and remaining at that level until the early hours of Oct 17.

## Singapore's central region recorded a PSI of 226 on Oct 16, in the very unhealthy range, as residents queued for N95 masks and schools adjusted routines.
Singapore's central region recorded a Pollutant Standards Index reading of 226 as of 10am on Friday (Oct 16), placing it in the very unhealthy range as haze conditions worsened. Residents across the island responded by collecting N95 masks, while schools adjusted routines to limit outdoor exposure.

## Haze PSI Reading Prompts Mask Collection


AsiaOne visited Toa Payoh MRT station at about 12.33pm on Friday, where just under 20 people were queuing to collect masks. The queue moved quickly, with a staff member assisting residents at the machines. Those waiting spent about five to seven minutes in the queue.

## Schools and Daily Routines Adjusted
The haze has also affected children's daily routines, with schools making adjustments to limit outdoor exposure. AsiaOne also visited the N95 mask distribution conducted at the Toa Payoh Central Community Club, where many parents brought their children after school to collect their masks.

Elliot Seah, 10, who collected a mask with his mother, said his school had moved recess into classrooms and stopped physical education lessons outdoors. He said these changes had begun the previous day, adding that students were eating in their classrooms instead of going outside. He described the smell as quite bad.
